options.C: A domain: member for Entra ID's sign-in domain.
options.D: A principalSet member for the pool's group a1b2c3.

explanation.summary: IAM names federated workforce identities with principal and principalSet identifiers; a group mapped through google.groups is addressed as principalSet://…/workforcePools/POOL/group/GROUP_ID.

option_breakdown.A: The group: prefix names Google groups in Cloud Identity; an Entra ID group isn't one.
option_breakdown.B: A workforce pool isn't a service account, and its users don't act as one.
option_breakdown.C: domain: grants to Google accounts in a Google-managed domain; it has nothing to do with Entra ID.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. IAM addresses federated workforce identities with principal and principalSet identifiers; a group mapped through google.groups is principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL/group/GROUP_ID.

questions.title: Where a workforce pool is created
questions.summary: Workforce identity pools are organisation-level resources in the global location.
questions.question: An administrator runs gcloud iam workforce-pools create hr-pool --project=hr-prod --location=europe-west4 and gets an error. The pool must let HR staff from the corporate IdP use Google Cloud. What is the correct way to create it?

options.A: In the same project, in the global location.
options.B: As a workload identity pool in project hr-prod.
options.C: Under the organisation, in the global location.
options.D: After enabling the IAM API in hr-prod, as before.

explanation.summary: Workforce identity pools are created at the organisation level and live in the global location; workload identity pools, for software, are the ones created in a project.

option_breakdown.A: A project is the wrong parent for a workforce pool, whatever the location.
option_breakdown.B: Workload identity pools federate software, not people signing in to the console.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Workforce identity pools are created at the organisation level and live in the global location; workload identity pools, for software, are the ones created in a project.
option_breakdown.D: The command fails on its parent and location, not on API enablement.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud iam workforce-pools create hr-pool --organization=ORG_ID --location=global \
  --display-name="HR staff"

questions.title: gcloud sign-in for federated users
questions.summary: Federated users sign in to gcloud with a login configuration file created for the workforce pool.
questions.question: Engineers already reach the console through a workforce identity pool. They now need to use gcloud from their laptops with the same federated identity, without Google accounts or service-account keys. What should you give them?

options.A: A JSON key for a shared service account that has their roles.
options.B: Instructions to run gcloud auth application-default login with personal Gmail accounts.
options.C: A Cloud Identity account each, synchronised from the IdP.
options.D: A gcloud login configuration file created for the pool.

explanation.summary: gcloud iam workforce-pools create-login-config produces a file that sends gcloud through the pool's federated sign-in, so engineers authenticate at their own IdP.

option_breakdown.A: A shared key is a long-lived secret and removes per-person attribution.
option_breakdown.B: Personal Gmail accounts are a different identity from the federated one IAM grants roles to.
option_breakdown.C: Workforce Identity Federation exists so that users need not be copied into Cloud Identity.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. gcloud iam workforce-pools create-login-config produces a file that sends gcloud through the pool's federated sign-in, so engineers authenticate at their own IdP.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud iam workforce-pools create-login-config \
  locations/global/workforcePools/corp-pool/providers/entra --output-file=login.json
gcloud auth login --login-config=login.json

questions.title: Which project should hold the metrics scope
questions.summary: Use a dedicated scoping project, free of workloads, and add the monitored projects to its metrics scope.
questions.question: Twelve production projects must appear in one set of dashboards and alerting policies managed by the SRE team. The team does not want its monitoring configuration mixed with any application's resources or access. How should you set this up?

options.A: A dedicated monitoring project whose metrics scope includes the twelve.
options.B: Add eleven projects to the metrics scope of the busiest production project.
options.C: Create dashboards separately in each project and link them with bookmarks.
options.D: Export every project's metrics to BigQuery and build dashboards there.

explanation.summary: A metrics scope lets one scoping project view and alert on many monitored projects; keeping that project free of workloads keeps monitoring access separate from application access.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A metrics scope lets one scoping project view and alert on many monitored projects; keeping that project free of workloads keeps monitoring access separate from application access.
option_breakdown.B: It works, but anyone with access to that application project gains the SRE view, and the two concerns are mixed.
option_breakdown.C: Twelve separate sets of dashboards and alerts are what a metrics scope removes.
option_breakdown.D: Monitoring metrics are not exported to BigQuery for dashboarding; this rebuilds Monitoring by hand.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Monitoring > Settings > Metrics scope > Add projects (in the dedicated scoping project)

questions.title: Keep new log buckets in the EU by default
questions.summary: Logging default resource settings set the storage location for _Default buckets created in new projects.
questions.question: A company's data-residency rules require that logs from every project created from now on are stored in europe-west4, including the _Default and _Required buckets that Logging creates automatically. What should you configure once?

options.A: An aggregated sink at the organisation that copies all logs to a bucket in europe-west4.
options.B: The gcp.resourceLocations organisation policy with only europe-west4 allowed.
options.C: Logging's default settings on the organisation, set to europe-west4.
options.D: A lifecycle rule on each project's log buckets that moves them to europe-west4.

explanation.summary: Default resource settings for Cloud Logging, set at the organisation or folder, decide where the automatically created log buckets of new projects are stored.

option_breakdown.A: A sink adds a copy elsewhere; the original buckets are still created in the global location.
option_breakdown.B: The resource-locations constraint governs resources that users create; it does not choose where Logging puts its automatic buckets.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Default resource settings for Cloud Logging, set at the organisation or folder, decide where the automatically created log buckets of new projects are stored.
option_breakdown.D: Log buckets cannot be moved between locations, and lifecycle rules are a Cloud Storage feature.

questions.title: A GPU quota error despite a regional increase
questions.summary: GPUs are limited by both a per-region quota and an all-regions quota; both must allow the request.
questions.question: A project was granted 16 NVIDIA L4 GPUs in us-central1. Creating eight 2-GPU VMs there still fails with a quota error naming GPUS_ALL_REGIONS, whose limit is 4. What should you do?

options.A: Create the VMs in a second project, which has its own GPU quota.
options.B: Request an increase of the GPUS_ALL_REGIONS quota.
options.C: Request a further increase of the us-central1 L4 quota.
options.D: Switch the VMs to Spot provisioning, which is not counted against GPU quotas.

explanation.summary: GPU capacity is bounded by the regional quota for the model and by a separate global GPU quota; the error names the global one, so that is the quota to raise.

option_breakdown.A: Spreading work across projects to dodge a quota is the distractor; the workload belongs in this project.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. GPU capacity is bounded by the regional quota for the model and by a separate global GPU quota; the error names the global one, so that is the quota to raise.
option_breakdown.C: The regional quota already allows 16; the error names the all-regions quota.
option_breakdown.D: Spot GPUs have their own quota metrics; switching does not remove the need for quota.

questions.title: Which APIs are switched on in a project
questions.summary: gcloud services list --enabled shows every API enabled in a project.
questions.question: During a security review, you must list every API currently enabled in project legacy-etl, so that unused ones can be turned off. What should you look at?

options.A: The project's services, filtered to those that are enabled.
options.B: The services available to the project.
options.C: The project's description from Resource Manager.
options.D: The project's quotas page.

explanation.summary: gcloud services list --enabled returns the services that are enabled on the project; the unused ones can then be turned off with gcloud services disable.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. gcloud services list --enabled returns the services enabled on the project, and unused ones can then be turned off with gcloud services disable.
option_breakdown.B: Available services are every API that could be enabled, hundreds of them, most of them off.
option_breakdown.C: The description shows the project's ID, number, parent and state, not its APIs.
option_breakdown.D: Quotas exist for many services whether or not you use them, so they don't show what is enabled.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud services list --enabled --project=legacy-etl
gcloud services disable SERVICE_NAME --project=legacy-etl

questions.title: An engineer leaves today; keep the data
questions.summary: Suspending a Cloud Identity user revokes sign-in and sessions at once while keeping the account's data.
questions.question: An engineer resigned and must lose all Google Cloud access immediately, across every project, including access through groups. Their manager still needs the files they own for a two-week handover. What should the administrator do?

options.A: Suspend the user in the Admin console.
options.B: Delete the user in the Admin console.
options.C: Remove the user's IAM bindings in each project, one by one.
options.D: Reset the user's password and email them the new one.

explanation.summary: Suspension blocks sign-in and revokes sessions and tokens at once, which makes every IAM binding — direct or through groups — unusable, while the account's data stays available for transfer.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Suspension blocks sign-in and revokes sessions and tokens at once, which makes every IAM binding — direct or through groups — unusable, while the account's data stays available for transfer.
option_breakdown.B: Deletion also ends access, but it starts removing the account and its data before the handover is done.
option_breakdown.C: Removing bindings one by one is slow, misses group memberships, and leaves the account able to sign in.
option_breakdown.D: A new password handed to the leaver keeps their access alive.

questions.title: Seeing what a constraint would block before enforcing it
questions.summary: A dry-run organisation policy reports violations without blocking anything.
questions.question: The security team plans to restrict resource locations to the EU at the organisation node, but several teams may already deploy to other regions. They want to see which operations the constraint would deny for two weeks before it blocks anyone. What should they do?

options.A: Enforce the policy on a Friday evening and roll it back if anyone complains.
options.B: Enforce the policy on one test project only.
options.C: Use Policy Troubleshooter for each team's service account.
options.D: Create the policy in dry-run mode and review its violation logs.

explanation.summary: A dry-run policy is evaluated alongside the live one and logs what it would have denied, without denying anything — the safe way to measure impact before enforcement.

option_breakdown.A: Enforcing first discovers the impact by breaking deployments.
option_breakdown.B: One test project says nothing about what the other teams deploy.
option_breakdown.C: Policy Troubleshooter explains IAM access decisions, not organisation-policy constraints.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A dry-run policy is evaluated alongside the live one and logs what it would have denied, without denying anything — the safe way to measure impact before enforcement.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud org-policies set-policy policy.yaml   # policy.yaml carries a dryRunSpec for gcp.resourceLocations

questions.title: A budget only for BigQuery in the analytics projects
questions.summary: A budget's scope can filter by projects and services, so it tracks just the spend that matters.
questions.question: Finance wants an alert when BigQuery spend in the three analytics projects reaches 80% of 4,000 EUR per month. Spend on other services and in other projects must not count towards it. What should you create?

options.A: A budget on the billing account with no scope filter, alerting at 80%.
options.B: A budget scoped to the three projects and BigQuery, alerting at 80%.
options.C: A custom quota of 4,000 EUR on BigQuery in each project.
options.D: A billing report filtered to BigQuery, bookmarked for finance.

explanation.summary: Budgets can be scoped to selected projects, services and labels, so the threshold tracks exactly the BigQuery spend of those projects.

option_breakdown.A: An unscoped budget counts every service in every linked project.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Budgets can be scoped to selected projects, services and labels, so the threshold tracks exactly the BigQuery spend of those projects.
option_breakdown.C: Quotas limit usage units, not currency, and would stop queries rather than alert.
option_breakdown.D: A report is something to look at; it notifies nobody.

questions.title: A budget that follows last month's spend
questions.summary: A budget amount can be set to last month's spend instead of a fixed figure.
questions.question: A product's cloud spend grows every month, and its owners want to know when this month's spend is on track to exceed last month's, without someone updating a fixed amount every month. How should the budget be configured?

options.A: Set a fixed amount and have finance edit it on the first of each month.
options.B: Create twelve budgets, one per calendar month, in advance.
options.C: Set the amount to last month's spend, alerting on forecasted spend at 100%.
options.D: Use the billing export and a monthly scheduled query that compares totals.

explanation.summary: The last-month's-spend amount type recalculates the target every month, and a forecasted-spend rule warns before the month closes.

option_breakdown.A: A manual monthly edit will be forgotten.
option_breakdown.B: Budgets reset each period; twelve of them is duplication, and each would still need a fixed amount.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The last-month's-spend amount type recalculates the target every month, and a forecasted-spend rule warns before the month closes.
option_breakdown.D: A scheduled query reports after the fact and sends nothing unless you build the alerting yourself.

questions.title: Budget alerts to the on-call chat channel
questions.summary: Budgets can send alerts to Cloud Monitoring notification channels such as chat, SMS or PagerDuty.
questions.question: Budget threshold emails go only to billing administrators, who rarely read them. The platform team wants the same alerts in its existing on-call chat channel, which is already a Cloud Monitoring notification channel. No automated action is required. What should you do?

options.A: Publish budget notifications to Pub/Sub and write a function that posts to the chat channel.
options.B: Add every platform engineer as a Billing Account Administrator.
options.C: Create a Cloud Monitoring uptime check on the billing console.
options.D: Link the budget to the existing Cloud Monitoring notification channel.

explanation.summary: A budget can notify up to several Cloud Monitoring notification channels directly, so an existing chat channel receives the threshold alerts with no code.

option_breakdown.A: Pub/Sub and a function are for programmatic responses; here they rebuild a built-in integration.
option_breakdown.B: Billing Administrator is a powerful role granted only to receive email — far beyond the need.
option_breakdown.C: An uptime check probes an endpoint; it knows nothing about spend.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A budget can notify up to several Cloud Monitoring notification channels directly, so an existing chat channel receives the threshold alerts with no code.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Billing > Budgets & alerts > (budget) > Manage notifications > Link Monitoring notification channels

questions.title: Cost of each individual VM
questions.summary: Only the detailed usage cost export carries resource-level rows such as which VM incurred a cost.
questions.question: Finance at Mariner Logistics already receives the standard usage cost export in BigQuery, broken down by project and SKU. They now need each month's cost for every individual Compute Engine instance, identified by its resource name, to charge back to the fleet owners. What should you enable?

options.A: The pricing export to BigQuery.
options.B: Labels on each project with the project owner's name.
options.C: A budget per instance with a threshold at 100%.
options.D: The detailed usage cost export to BigQuery.

explanation.summary: The detailed usage cost export includes everything in the standard export plus resource-level rows, so costs can be grouped by individual instance.

option_breakdown.A: The pricing export contains list and contract prices, not usage.
option_breakdown.B: Project labels attribute cost per project, which finance already has.
option_breakdown.C: Budgets notify on thresholds; they do not produce per-resource cost data.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The detailed usage cost export includes everything in the standard export plus resource-level rows, so costs can be grouped by individual instance.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Billing > Billing export > BigQuery export > Detailed usage cost > Edit settings

questions.title: Comparing list prices with negotiated prices
questions.summary: The pricing export to BigQuery holds list and contract prices for SKU-level price analysis.
questions.question: Procurement wants to query, in SQL, the list price and the company's negotiated contract price of every SKU it uses, to prepare a contract renewal. Usage data is already exported. What should you add?

options.A: The detailed usage cost export to BigQuery.
options.B: The Google Cloud Pricing Calculator, with a saved estimate.
options.C: The pricing data export to BigQuery on the billing account.
options.D: A budget report grouped by SKU.

explanation.summary: The pricing export writes the billing account's list prices and contract prices per SKU to BigQuery, where they can be queried and joined with the usage export.

option_breakdown.A: The detailed export adds resource-level usage rows, not a price list.
option_breakdown.B: The calculator prices a planned configuration at list price; it does not hold negotiated prices as data.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The pricing export writes the billing account's list prices and contract prices per SKU to BigQuery, where they can be queried and joined with the usage export.
option_breakdown.D: Reports show spend, not the price book.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Billing > Billing export > Pricing > Edit settings (choose project and dataset)

questions.title: What a firewall rule looked like ten days ago
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory keeps a 35-day history of asset metadata and IAM policies.
questions.question: You need to see what the configuration of the firewall rule allow-admin looked like ten days ago, before someone widened its source range. No feeds or exports were ever configured. What can you use?

options.A: The rule's asset history in Cloud Asset Inventory.
options.B: Firewall Insights for the rule.
options.C: VPC Flow Logs for the subnets the rule applies to.
options.D: A new Cloud Asset Inventory feed for firewall rules.

explanation.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory keeps five weeks of history for resource metadata and IAM policies, so get-history returns earlier versions without any setup.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Cloud Asset Inventory keeps five weeks of history for resource metadata and IAM policies, so the rule's history (gcloud asset get-history) returns earlier versions without any setup.
option_breakdown.B: Firewall Insights reports shadowed and unused rules and hit counts, not earlier configurations.
option_breakdown.C: Flow logs record traffic, not a rule's configuration, and nobody enabled them.
option_breakdown.D: Feeds send notifications for future changes only.

questions.title: Federated group grants that never apply
questions.summary: Map the IdP's group claim to google.groups; otherwise principalSet group bindings match nobody.
questions.question: Users sign in to the console through a workforce pool connected to the company's OIDC IdP. A role granted to principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/corp/group/finance has no effect, although the IdP token includes a groups claim listing finance. What is most likely missing?

options.A: A Cloud Identity group named finance.
options.B: Google Cloud Directory Sync for the IdP's groups.
options.C: An attribute condition that allows the finance group.
options.D: A google.groups attribute mapping from the token's groups claim.

explanation.summary: Group bindings in a workforce pool match the google.groups attribute. Unless the provider maps the IdP's groups claim into it, the group principal set is empty.

option_breakdown.A: Workforce Identity Federation needs no Cloud Identity groups; that is the point of federating.
option_breakdown.B: No synchronisation is needed; groups come from the token at sign-in.
option_breakdown.C: Attribute conditions reject tokens; they do not populate group membership.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Group bindings in a workforce pool match the google.groups attribute. Unless the provider maps the IdP's groups claim into it, the group principal set is empty.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud iam workforce-pools providers update-oidc corp-idp --workforce-pool=corp --location=global \
  --attribute-mapping="google.subject=assertion.sub,google.groups=assertion.groups"

questions.title: Shorter console sessions for federated contractors
questions.summary: The workforce pool's session duration (15 minutes to 12 hours, default 1 hour) controls federated sessions.
questions.question: Contractors reach the Google Cloud console through a dedicated workforce pool. Security wants their console and gcloud sessions to expire after 30 minutes, without affecting employees in another pool. What should you change?

options.A: Set the contractors' workforce pool session duration to 1800s.
options.B: Set the Google Workspace session length to 30 minutes.
options.C: Add an IAM condition that expires the contractors' role bindings after 30 minutes.
options.D: Lower the OAuth access-token lifetime organisation policy to 30 minutes.

explanation.summary: A workforce pool's session duration controls how long access tokens and console and gcloud sessions from that pool are valid. It can be set per pool between 15 minutes and 12 hours.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A workforce pool's session duration controls how long access tokens and console and gcloud sessions from that pool are valid. It can be set per pool between 15 minutes and 12 hours.
option_breakdown.B: Workspace session controls apply to Google accounts, not federated workforce identities.
option_breakdown.C: A time-based condition removes access at a fixed date; it does not limit session length.
option_breakdown.D: That constraint governs service-account token lifetime extension, not federated user sessions.

questions.title: Which projects actually enforce a constraint
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory's organisation policy analysis reports the effective policy on every resource.
questions.question: Folders and projects across the organisation set, override and inherit the constraint compute.vmExternalIpAccess in different ways. A security lead needs a list of every project and the effective policy it ends up with. What is the quickest way?

options.A: Describe the policy on every project, one at a time, in a loop.
options.B: Organisation policy analysis in Cloud Asset Inventory.
options.C: Admin Activity audit logs filtered on SetOrgPolicy calls.
options.D: A Cloud Asset Inventory search of IAM policies for the constraint.

explanation.summary: Organisation policy analysis in Cloud Asset Inventory evaluates inheritance and overrides and returns the effective policy for each resource in scope, in one call.

option_breakdown.A: It works, but it is slow across a whole organisation, and it shows only what is set on each project unless you ask for the effective policy.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Organisation policy analysis (gcloud asset analyze-org-policies) evaluates inheritance and overrides and returns the effective policy for every resource in scope, in one call.
option_breakdown.C: Audit logs show changes that happened, not the resulting effective policy everywhere.
option_breakdown.D: That searches IAM allow policies, not organisation policies.

questions.title: Checking what breaks before moving a project
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: gcloud asset analyze-move reports IAM and organisation policy effects of moving a project.
questions.question: You plan to move project billing-api from the Sandbox folder to the Production folder, whose organisation policies and inherited IAM grants are different. Before moving it, you want a report of the policy and access changes the move would cause. What should you run?

options.A: Move the project, then move it back if something breaks.
options.B: Export both folders' IAM policies and compare them by hand.
options.C: Cloud Asset Inventory's move analysis for the project.
options.D: Read the Production folder's own IAM policy.

explanation.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory's move analysis evaluates the destination's organisation policies and IAM inheritance for the project and reports what would change.

option_breakdown.A: That finds the impact by causing it.
option_breakdown.B: Manual comparison is slow and misses organisation policy effects.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Move analysis (gcloud asset analyze-move) evaluates the destination's organisation policies and IAM inheritance for the project and reports what would change.
option_breakdown.D: That shows the folder's own bindings only, not the effect on the project.

questions.title: SQL over the resource inventory without an export pipeline
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: gcloud asset query runs SQL over Cloud Asset Inventory data directly.
questions.question: An engineer wants to run a SQL query that counts Compute Engine disks by type and zone across the organisation. No BigQuery export has been set up, and this is a one-off question. What can they use?

options.A: Cloud Asset Inventory's SQL query over current asset data.
options.B: A disk listing per project, combined in a spreadsheet.
options.C: A Cloud Asset Inventory feed to Pub/Sub.
options.D: Log Analytics on the Admin Activity audit logs.

explanation.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory can run SQL queries over current (or recent) asset data without a user-managed BigQuery export.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Cloud Asset Inventory can run SQL (gcloud asset query) over current or recent asset data without a BigQuery export you manage.
option_breakdown.B: That lists disks for one project at a time and needs manual aggregation.
option_breakdown.C: Feeds notify about future changes; they do not answer queries.
option_breakdown.D: Audit logs record operations, not a complete inventory of existing disks.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud asset query --organization=ORG_ID --statement=\
  "SELECT resource.data.type, resource.location, COUNT(*) FROM compute_googleapis_com_Disk GROUP BY 1, 2"

questions.title: Only employees, not guests, may federate
questions.summary: An attribute condition on the workforce provider rejects tokens that do not meet it.
questions.question: A workforce pool trusts the company's Microsoft Entra ID tenant, which also holds guest accounts for suppliers. Only employees, whose tokens carry an employee_type claim of "staff", may sign in to Google Cloud at all. What should you configure?

options.A: An IAM deny policy for guests on every project.
options.B: An attribute condition on the provider requiring employee_type staff.
options.C: A google.groups mapping that excludes guests.
options.D: A shorter session duration on the pool.

explanation.summary: An attribute condition is evaluated at token exchange. Tokens that do not satisfy it are rejected, so guests cannot obtain a Google Cloud session at all.

option_breakdown.A: Deny policies block permissions after sign-in and must be maintained everywhere.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. An attribute condition is evaluated at token exchange. Tokens that do not satisfy it are rejected, so guests cannot obtain a Google Cloud session at all.
option_breakdown.C: Group mapping controls which groups users appear in, not whether they may federate.
option_breakdown.D: Session length has nothing to do with who may sign in.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud iam workforce-pools providers update-oidc entra --workforce-pool=corp --location=global \
  --attribute-condition="assertion.employee_type == 'staff'"

questions.title: Cutting off every federated user at once
questions.summary: Disabling a workforce pool stops all its users from signing in and obtaining new tokens.
questions.question: During a security incident at a contractor's identity provider, you must immediately stop every user federated through the contractors workforce pool from accessing Google Cloud, without deleting the pool or its IAM bindings. What should you do?

options.A: Remove every principalSet binding for the pool from all projects.
options.B: Ask the contractor to reset all passwords.
options.C: Disable the contractors workforce pool.
options.D: Set the pool's session duration to 15 minutes.

explanation.summary: A disabled workforce pool cannot be used to sign in or to exchange tokens, and it can be re-enabled later with its providers and bindings intact.

option_breakdown.A: Removing bindings is slow, error-prone and has to be undone by hand afterwards.
option_breakdown.B: Password resets happen outside your control and do not end existing sessions.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A disabled workforce pool cannot be used to sign in or to exchange tokens, and it can be re-enabled later with its providers and bindings intact.
option_breakdown.D: Existing sessions could still run up to 15 minutes, and new sign-ins still succeed.

questions.title: A role for everyone in one department, by attribute
questions.summary: Map a custom attribute and grant to principalSet://.../attribute.NAME/VALUE.
questions.question: Federated users' tokens include a department claim, but the IdP has no groups for departments. Everyone whose department is finance needs BigQuery Data Viewer on the finance project. How should you grant it?

options.A: A Cloud Identity group named finance, with each user added.
options.B: A principalSet for every user in the pool.
options.C: Each finance user's own principal identifier.
options.D: A department attribute mapped on the provider, granted as a principalSet.

explanation.summary: Custom attributes mapped from the token can be used as principal sets in IAM, so the grant follows the department claim as it changes in the IdP.

option_breakdown.A: Federated users are not Cloud Identity users and cannot be added to Cloud Identity groups.
option_breakdown.B: The pool-wide principalSet (…/workforcePools/corp/*) grants the role to every user of the pool.
option_breakdown.C: Per-user grants need maintenance on every change.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Map attribute.department=assertion.department, then grant to principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/corp/attribute.department/finance; the grant follows the claim as it changes in the IdP.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud iam workforce-pools providers update-oidc entra --workforce-pool=corp --location=global \
  --attribute-mapping="google.subject=assertion.sub,attribute.department=assertion.department"

questions.title: Which Spanner dual-region configurations exist
questions.summary: List Spanner instance configurations to see which regional, dual-region and multi-region options exist.
questions.question: Before committing to an architecture, you need to confirm which Spanner dual-region configurations are available to your project. What is the most direct check?

options.A: The list of Compute Engine regions and zones.
options.B: The Spanner instances that already exist in the project.
options.C: The Spanner instance configurations available to the project.
options.D: The Spanner API's entry in the project's available services.

explanation.summary: Instance configurations define where Spanner can place replicas. Listing them shows the regional, dual-region and multi-region configurations you can use.

option_breakdown.A: Compute Engine regions don't tell you which Spanner configurations exist.
option_breakdown.B: That lists instances you already created, not the configurations you could choose.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Instance configurations define where Spanner can place replicas; listing them (gcloud spanner instance-configs list) shows the regional, dual-region and multi-region configurations you can use.
option_breakdown.D: That only tells you the Spanner API can be enabled.

questions.title: EU residency plus EU-only support personnel
questions.summary: Assured Workloads applies a control package (data location and personnel controls) to a folder.
questions.question: A public-sector customer requires that its data stays in the EU and that only EU-based Google support personnel can access it, with these controls applied to every project in its workload. What should you set up?

options.A: The gcp.resourceLocations organisation policy set to in:eu-locations.
options.B: Projects in europe-west regions with CMEK.
options.C: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the projects.
options.D: An Assured Workloads folder with an EU data boundary control package.

explanation.summary: Assured Workloads creates a folder with a control package that enforces data location and restricts support personnel, and it monitors for violations.

option_breakdown.A: The location constraint covers where resources are created, not who at Google may support them.
option_breakdown.B: Region and key choices do not control support personnel access.
option_breakdown.C: A service perimeter limits data exfiltration over APIs; it says nothing about personnel.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Assured Workloads creates a folder with a control package that enforces data location and restricts support personnel, and it monitors for violations.

questions.title: Reading logs from several projects in one Logs Explorer view
questions.summary: A log scope groups log views and projects so Logs Explorer can query them together.
questions.question: An SRE investigates incidents that span three projects and keeps switching projects in Logs Explorer. Logs stay in each project's own buckets. How can the SRE query all three together in one view?

options.A: A log scope with the three projects, selected in Logs Explorer.
options.B: Create a metrics scope that includes the three projects.
options.C: Route all logs from the three projects into a fourth project.
options.D: Grant the SRE Logs Viewer on the organisation.

explanation.summary: A log scope defines a set of projects and log views that Logs Explorer queries together, without moving any logs.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A log scope defines a set of projects and log views that Logs Explorer queries together, without moving any logs.
option_breakdown.B: Metrics scopes cover metrics and dashboards, not Logs Explorer queries.
option_breakdown.C: Centralising works but changes storage and routing, which the stem does not want.
option_breakdown.D: More permission does not make Logs Explorer search several projects at once.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Logging > Log scopes > Create log scope > add the three projects

questions.title: Quota that grows with usage without tickets
questions.summary: The quota adjuster watches usage and requests increases automatically for supported quotas.
questions.question: A fast-growing project keeps hitting supported Compute Engine quotas, and each time an engineer files a quota increase request by hand. The team wants increases requested automatically as usage approaches the limit. What should it enable?

options.A: A budget alert at 90% of the quota value.
options.B: An organisation policy that removes quota limits.
options.C: The quota adjuster in Cloud Quotas.
options.D: A committed use discount for the vCPUs.

explanation.summary: The quota adjuster monitors usage of supported quotas and submits increase requests when usage approaches the current value. It only raises quotas.

option_breakdown.A: Budgets track spend, not quota usage, and request nothing.
option_breakdown.B: No organisation policy removes quotas.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The quota adjuster monitors usage of supported quotas and submits increase requests when usage approaches the current value. It only raises quotas.
option_breakdown.D: Commitments lower prices; they do not change quota.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > IAM & Admin > Quotas & System Limits > Configure > Quota adjuster: Enabled

questions.title: A warning before a quota runs out
questions.summary: Create a Cloud Monitoring alert on quota usage (from the Quotas page) at a threshold such as 80%.
questions.question: A regional quota for GPUs in a training project must never be exhausted by surprise. The team wants an email when usage passes 80% of the quota. What should it create?

options.A: A Cloud Billing budget with an 80% threshold.
options.B: An uptime check on the Compute Engine API.
options.C: A log-based metric on quota-exceeded errors.
options.D: A quota usage alert at 80%, created from the Quotas page.

explanation.summary: Quota usage is exported as Cloud Monitoring metrics, and an alerting policy on usage against the limit warns before the quota is reached.

option_breakdown.A: Budgets watch money, not quota usage.
option_breakdown.B: Uptime checks test endpoints, not quotas.
option_breakdown.C: An error-based metric only fires after requests have already failed.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Quota usage is exported as Cloud Monitoring metrics, and an alerting policy on usage against the limit warns before the quota is reached.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Quotas & System Limits > select the quota > Create usage alert (threshold 80%)

questions.title: A rule no predefined constraint expresses
questions.summary: Custom organisation policy constraints use CEL conditions on resource fields of supported services.
questions.question: Security wants every new GKE cluster in the organisation to have Workload Identity Federation for GKE enabled. No predefined constraint does this. What should you use?

options.A: An IAM deny policy on container.clusters.create.
options.B: A custom constraint, enforced by an organisation policy.
options.C: A Cloud Asset Inventory feed that deletes non-compliant clusters.
options.D: A tag on the organisation named workload-identity=required.

explanation.summary: Custom constraints evaluate conditions on the fields of supported resources when they are created or updated, and deny requests that do not comply.

option_breakdown.A: A deny policy blocks the permission for everyone; it cannot inspect the cluster's configuration.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Custom constraints evaluate conditions on the fields of supported resources when they are created or updated, and deny requests that do not comply.
option_breakdown.C: Deleting after the fact is detective and disruptive, not preventive.
option_breakdown.D: A tag by itself enforces nothing.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-custom-constraint wi-required.yaml   # CEL on resource.workloadIdentityConfig
gcloud org-policies set-policy enforce-wi.yaml

questions.title: No Cloud SQL instance may have a public IP
questions.summary: The sql.restrictPublicIp constraint prevents public IP configuration on Cloud SQL instances.
questions.question: After an audit finding, the organisation must ensure that no team can create or update a Cloud SQL instance with a public IP address. What should be enforced at the organisation node?

options.A: The constraint compute.vmExternalIpAccess.
options.B: The constraint sql.restrictAuthorizedNetworks.
options.C: A hierarchical firewall policy that denies ingress to port 3306.
options.D: The constraint sql.restrictPublicIp.

explanation.summary: sql.restrictPublicIp blocks configuring public IP on Cloud SQL instances in the hierarchy below where it is enforced.

option_breakdown.A: That constraint applies to Compute Engine VM external IPs, not Cloud SQL.
option_breakdown.B: That restricts adding authorised networks, while still allowing a public IP.
option_breakdown.C: Firewall policies do not govern Cloud SQL's public IP, and not every engine uses 3306.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. sql.restrictPublicIp blocks configuring public IP on Cloud SQL instances in the hierarchy below where it is enforced.

questions.title: Users created automatically from Microsoft Entra ID
questions.summary: Entra ID's Google Cloud provisioning connector (SCIM-style) creates and suspends Cloud Identity users.
questions.question: A company runs Microsoft Entra ID (not on-premises Active Directory) and needs Cloud Identity users to be created, updated and suspended automatically when employees join, move or leave. What should it set up?

options.A: Automatic provisioning from Entra ID's Google Cloud enterprise app.
options.B: Google Cloud Directory Sync on a domain controller.
options.C: A workforce identity pool, which creates Cloud Identity users.
options.D: A nightly CSV upload in the Admin console.

explanation.summary: Entra ID can provision and deprovision users and groups into Cloud Identity through its enterprise application, and SSO can be configured alongside it.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Entra ID can provision and deprovision users and groups into Cloud Identity through its enterprise application, and SSO can be configured alongside it.
option_breakdown.B: GCDS synchronises from LDAP directories such as on-premises Active Directory.
option_breakdown.C: Workforce Identity Federation deliberately avoids creating Cloud Identity users.
option_breakdown.D: Manual uploads are not automatic and miss leavers.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > Google Cloud > Provisioning: Automatic

questions.title: Switching between two environments in gcloud
questions.summary: Named gcloud configurations hold account, project and region; activate one to switch them all.
questions.question: An engineer alternates between a staging project with one account and a production project with another account and a different default region. They keep running commands against the wrong project. What should they set up?

options.A: Two named gcloud configurations, activated to switch between them.
options.B: Two installations of the Google Cloud CLI.
options.C: An environment variable per command with --project.
options.D: A service account key for each project.

explanation.summary: A named configuration stores a set of properties such as account, project and compute/region. Activating one switches all of them together.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A named configuration stores a set of properties such as account, project and compute/region. Activating one switches all of them together.
option_breakdown.B: Separate installations are unnecessary and hard to maintain.
option_breakdown.C: Per-command flags are exactly the error-prone habit to remove.
option_breakdown.D: Keys add risk and do not change default properties.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud config configurations create prod
gcloud config set project shop-prod && gcloud config set account ana@example.com
gcloud config configurations activate staging

questions.title: Spotting an unusual spend spike without setting thresholds
questions.summary: Cloud Billing cost anomaly detection flags spikes against historical patterns with no setup.
questions.question: A finance analyst wants to be told when a project's spend suddenly deviates from its usual pattern, without guessing a fixed threshold for each of 200 projects. What should they use?

options.A: A budget per project at 100% of last year's average.
options.B: A billing export to BigQuery with a weekly manual review.
options.C: Committed use discount recommendations.
options.D: Cost anomaly detection in Cloud Billing, with alerts.

explanation.summary: Anomaly detection compares spend with historical patterns across the billing account's projects and surfaces unexpected spikes, without per-project thresholds.

option_breakdown.A: Fixed budgets need a threshold per project and miss changes below it.
option_breakdown.B: A weekly manual review is slow and relies on people.
option_breakdown.C: Commitment recommendations are about discounts, not spikes.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Anomaly detection compares spend with historical patterns across the billing account's projects and surfaces unexpected spikes, without per-project thresholds.

questions.title: Removing one person's grant from a busy policy
questions.summary: remove-iam-policy-binding takes out exactly one member–role pair and leaves every other binding alone.
questions.question: A contractor's engagement has ended, and their Viewer role on project ops-prod must be removed from the project's IAM policy. Other teams' automation edits the same policy throughout the day, and their bindings must not change. What should you do?

options.A: Write a policy file without the contractor and apply it with set-iam-policy.
options.B: Add an IAM deny policy for the contractor on the project.
options.C: Run remove-iam-policy-binding for the contractor and the Viewer role.
options.D: Delete the contractor's Google account from the project's IAM page.

explanation.summary: remove-iam-policy-binding reads, modifies and writes the policy for you, removing exactly one member from one role and leaving every other binding as it is.

option_breakdown.A: Replacing the whole policy from a file can overwrite changes other automation made after you read it.
option_breakdown.B: A deny policy blocks the permissions, but the grant stays in the allow policy, which isn't what was asked.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. It removes only that member–role pair, with the read-modify-write handled by gcloud.
option_breakdown.D: You can't delete someone's Google account from a project; you can only change the project's IAM bindings.

questions.title: Default region and zone for every gcloud command
questions.summary: gcloud properties compute/region and compute/zone set the defaults that commands use when no location flag is given.
questions.question: An engineer works almost entirely in europe-west4-b and is tired of adding --zone to every Compute Engine command. What should they do so that commands use that zone unless told otherwise?

options.A: Export the CLOUDSDK_CONFIG variable with the zone name.
options.B: Set the compute/zone and compute/region properties in the active configuration.
options.C: Create the project's resources in that zone, which gcloud then remembers.
options.D: Set the default zone on the project's billing account.

explanation.summary: gcloud reads defaults such as compute/zone and compute/region from the active configuration, and a --zone flag on a command still overrides them.

option_breakdown.A: CLOUDSDK_CONFIG points gcloud at a configuration directory; it doesn't hold a zone.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. With these properties set, commands that need a location use them by default.
option_breakdown.C: gcloud doesn't infer defaults from where resources were created.
option_breakdown.D: Billing accounts have no location settings for the CLI.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud config set compute/region europe-west4
gcloud config set compute/zone europe-west4-b

questions.title: One command against a different project
questions.summary: The --project flag runs a single command against another project without changing the active configuration.
questions.question: Your active gcloud configuration points at project shop-dev. You need to list the VMs in project shop-prod once, without changing what later commands use. What should you run?

options.A: gcloud config set project shop-prod, then list the instances.
options.B: gcloud auth login as a user who owns shop-prod, then list the instances.
options.C: A new gcloud configuration for shop-prod, activated for the command.
options.D: gcloud compute instances list with --project=shop-prod.

explanation.summary: Global flags such as --project override the configuration for one command only, leaving the active configuration unchanged.

option_breakdown.A: This changes the default for every later command, which the stem rules out.
option_breakdown.B: Logging in changes the account, not which project commands target.
option_breakdown.C: It works but is heavier than needed, and it changes the active configuration until you switch back.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. --project applies to that command alone.

questions.title: gcloud components update is refused
questions.summary: When the Google Cloud CLI was installed with a system package manager, it is updated through that package manager, not gcloud components.
questions.question: On an Ubuntu server, the Google Cloud CLI was installed from Google's apt repository. Running gcloud components update fails with a message that the component manager is disabled for this installation. How should you update the CLI?

options.A: Update it through apt, the package manager that installed it.
options.B: Run gcloud components update with sudo.
options.C: Delete ~/.config/gcloud and run the update again.
options.D: Reinstall the CLI from a tarball on top of the apt installation.

explanation.summary: Package-manager installations disable the component manager so that apt or yum stays in control; updates and extra components come from the same repository.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. apt-get update and an upgrade of google-cloud-cli (and its component packages) updates it.
option_breakdown.B: Root privileges don't re-enable a component manager that the installation disabled.
option_breakdown.C: That directory holds your configurations and credentials, not the installation's settings.
option_breakdown.D: Two installations side by side cause conflicts and confusion over which gcloud runs.

explanation.gcloud_command: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade google-cloud-cli

questions.title: Separate network hosts for production and the rest
questions.summary: A foundation usually has separate Shared VPC host projects for production and non-production, so the environments are isolated by design.
questions.question: A new organisation's foundation will use Shared VPC. Security requires that no misconfigured route or firewall rule in development or test can ever affect production traffic. How should the host projects be laid out?

options.A: One host project with one VPC, and one subnet per environment.
options.B: One host project per application team, shared by all its environments.
options.C: No Shared VPC: a separate VPC in every project, peered together.
options.D: A production host project and a separate non-production host project.

explanation.summary: Routes and firewall rules belong to a VPC. Separate host projects, each with its own VPC, mean a change in non-production can't reach production.

option_breakdown.A: Subnets in one VPC share its routes and firewall rules, so a mistake in one environment can affect another.
option_breakdown.B: Per-team hosts mix environments inside each team's network.
option_breakdown.C: Peering every project rebuilds the many-networks problem Shared VPC removes.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Each environment's network is a separate VPC with its own routes and rules, administered centrally.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute shared-vpc enable net-host-prod
gcloud compute shared-vpc enable net-host-nonprod

questions.title: A project whose billing account was closed
questions.summary: A project without an active billing account has billing disabled; linking it to an active account restores paid services.
questions.question: Finance closed an old billing account. A project that was still linked to it now has billing disabled, and its VMs have stopped. The project must keep running on the company's current billing account. What should you do?

options.A: Link the project to the active billing account.
options.B: Reopen the closed account under a new name.
options.C: Create a new project and move every resource into it.
options.D: Ask support to transfer the old account's credit to the project.

explanation.summary: A project needs an active billing account for paid services. Linking it to the current account re-enables billing; stopped resources can then be started again.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Linking (for example with gcloud billing projects link) restores billing for the project.
option_breakdown.B: A closed account isn't the company's current account, and reopening it isn't the fix that was asked for.
option_breakdown.C: Projects can't be merged, and moving resources is far more work than relinking.
option_breakdown.D: Credit isn't the issue; the project has no active billing account.

questions.title: Cost per Kubernetes namespace
questions.summary: GKE cost allocation adds namespace and Kubernetes label data to the detailed billing export.
questions.question: Five teams share one GKE Standard cluster, each in its own namespace. Finance already has the detailed billing export in BigQuery but sees only node costs. It needs cost per namespace. What should you enable?

options.A: A label on each node pool with the team's name.
options.B: A separate billing account for each team.
options.C: GKE cost allocation on the cluster.
options.D: A budget for each namespace in Cloud Billing.

explanation.summary: With GKE cost allocation, the billing export breaks cluster costs down by namespace and Kubernetes labels, based on the resources each workload requests.

option_breakdown.A: The teams share node pools, so node pool labels can't separate their costs.
option_breakdown.B: Billing accounts attach to projects, not namespaces.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Cost allocation adds namespace and label detail to the export rows.
option_breakdown.D: Budgets can't be scoped to a namespace, and they don't produce the cost breakdown.

questions.title: Incident logs gone before the review
questions.summary: The _Default log bucket keeps logs for 30 days by default, and its retention can be changed.
questions.question: An SRE preparing a review of an incident from seven weeks ago finds that the application's entries for that week are no longer in Logs Explorer, though they were never excluded. Reviews happen up to 90 days later. What should be changed so this doesn't happen again?

options.A: The _Required bucket's retention, to 90 days.
options.B: A sink to a Cloud Storage bucket kept for 90 days.
options.C: Data Access audit logs, turned on for the project.
options.D: The _Default bucket's retention, to 90 days.

explanation.summary: Logs that aren't audit or system logs go to the _Default bucket, whose 30-day default retention can be set to a longer period.

option_breakdown.A: The _Required bucket holds audit and system logs, and its retention can't be changed.
option_breakdown.B: A sink exports a copy outside Cloud Logging, which the stem rules out.
option_breakdown.C: Data Access logs add new entries; they don't change retention.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Updating the _Default bucket's retention keeps those logs for 90 days in place.

questions.title: Linking a new project to the company billing account
questions.summary: Linking a project to a billing account needs Billing Account User on the billing account and a role with billing-management permission on the project.
questions.question: A team lead at Sefton Print creates projects for new campaigns and must link each one to the company's billing account. They must not see invoices, change payment methods or manage other people's billing access. Which two roles should you grant? (Choose two.)

options.A: Billing Account User on the billing account
options.B: Project Billing Manager on the campaign projects, or on their folder
options.C: Billing Account Costs Manager on the billing account
options.D: Billing Account Viewer on the billing account
options.E: Billing Account Administrator on the billing account

explanation.summary: Linking needs permission on both sides: Billing Account User lets someone attach projects to the billing account, and Project Billing Manager (or Owner) on the project lets them change its billing link.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. It allows linking projects to the billing account, without access to invoices or payment settings.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. It lets the lead change the billing link of the projects they create.
option_breakdown.C: Costs Manager manages budgets and exports; it can't link projects either.
option_breakdown.D: Viewer shows costs and invoices but can't link projects.
option_breakdown.E: Administrator manages payment methods and billing IAM, which is ruled out.

questions.title: Budget alerts for a team that isn't in billing
questions.summary: A budget can be scoped to one project, and Cloud Monitoring notification channels send its alerts to people who have no billing role.
questions.question: The mobile team at Grayling Apps wants an alert when their project's monthly spend reaches 50%, 90% and 100% of $3,000. Nobody on the team has a billing role, and finance doesn't want to give them one. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Connect a Cloud Monitoring email notification channel for the team to the budget.
options.B: Set a Compute Engine quota that matches the $3,000 amount.
options.C: Create a budget scoped to the mobile project with thresholds at 50%, 90% and 100%.
options.D: Export billing data to BigQuery and ask the team to check it weekly.
options.E: Grant the mobile team Billing Account Administrator so they receive budget emails.

explanation.summary: Budgets can be filtered to a project, with several thresholds. By default only billing admins and users get the emails; linking Monitoring notification channels sends the alerts to anyone else.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A notification channel delivers the budget's alerts to the team without a billing role.
option_breakdown.B: Quotas limit resources, not spend, and they don't send budget alerts.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The budget tracks just the mobile project against $3,000 at the three thresholds.
option_breakdown.D: A weekly check isn't an alert, and spend could pass 100% between checks.
option_breakdown.E: This is the billing role finance won't give, and it's far broader than receiving alerts.

questions.title: Guardrails for service accounts in every new project
questions.summary: Two organization policy constraints cover the common service account risks: one blocks key creation, the other stops the automatic Editor grant to default service accounts.
questions.question: Security at Linfield Bank wants two guardrails in every project in the organization: nobody may create service account keys, and default service accounts must no longer receive the Editor role automatically when an API is enabled. Which two organization policy constraints should you enforce? (Choose two.)

options.A: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
options.B: compute.requireOsLogin on every project
options.C: iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains for the company
options.D: iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts

explanation.summary: Organization policies are inherited by every project. One boolean constraint blocks creating service account keys, and another stops default service accounts being granted Editor automatically.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. With it enforced, no one can create user-managed keys for service accounts.
option_breakdown.B: OS Login governs SSH access to VMs, not service accounts.
option_breakdown.C: Domain restricted sharing limits who can be granted roles; it doesn't stop keys or the Editor grant.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. It stops the automatic Editor grant to default service accounts in new projects.
option_breakdown.E: This blocks creating service accounts at all, which is far more than either guardrail asks.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager org-policies enable-enforce iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation --organization=ORG_ID
gcloud resource-manager org-policies enable-enforce iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts --organization=ORG_ID

questions.title: Searching every project for VMs with public addresses
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory searches resources across the whole organization; the searcher needs Cloud Asset Viewer at that scope.
questions.question: An auditor at Moreton Shipping must list every Compute Engine VM with an external IP address across the organization's 300 projects, today and on request later. They must not be able to change anything. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Search all resources at the organization scope for instances with an external IP.
options.B: Run gcloud compute instances list in each project with a script.
options.C: Enable VPC Flow Logs on every subnet and query them.
options.D: Grant the auditor Compute Admin on each of the 300 projects.
options.E: Grant the auditor Cloud Asset Viewer on the organization.

explanation.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory indexes resources and their configurations across the hierarchy. With Cloud Asset Viewer on the organization, one search covers every project, read-only.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A single organization-scope search returns every matching VM in all projects.
option_breakdown.B: A per-project loop needs access to each project and misses projects added later.
option_breakdown.C: Flow logs record traffic, not which VMs have external IPs, and enabling them is a change.
option_breakdown.D: Compute Admin can change and delete VMs, and granting it 300 times is error-prone.
option_breakdown.E: Correct. It is read-only and lets the auditor search assets across the organization.

questions.title: Letting an app project use the host network
questions.summary: Shared VPC needs the host project enabled and each service project attached to it; then Network User grants let service project teams use subnets.
questions.question: Haverley Foods is setting up its network foundation. The net-host project holds the company VPC, and the new orders project must create VMs in that VPC's subnets, while the network team keeps control of the network. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Copy the company VPC's subnets into the orders project.
options.B: Enable net-host as a Shared VPC host project.
options.C: Attach orders to net-host as a service project.
options.D: Create a VPC in orders and peer it with the company VPC.
options.E: Grant the orders team Compute Network Admin on net-host.

explanation.summary: In Shared VPC, a host project owns the network and service projects are attached to it. Service project teams then get Compute Network User on the subnets they may use, while the network team keeps administration.

option_breakdown.A: Subnets can't be copied between projects; a copy would be a separate network anyway.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The host project must be enabled before any project can use its network.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Attaching orders lets its resources use subnets of the host's VPC once granted.
option_breakdown.D: Peering joins two separately run networks; the orders VMs wouldn't be in the company VPC's subnets.
option_breakdown.E: Network Admin hands network control to the app team, which the network team must keep.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute shared-vpc enable net-host
gcloud compute shared-vpc associated-projects add orders --host-project=net-host

questions.title: Warning before a quota runs out
questions.summary: The Quotas page shows usage against each limit, and a Cloud Monitoring alert on the quota usage metrics warns before a limit is reached.
questions.question: Last month Pennard Labs hit its regional GPU quota in the middle of a training run. The team wants to see current usage against each quota, and to be warned automatically when any GPU quota passes 80% of its limit. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Turn on Data Access audit logs for Compute Engine.
options.B: Create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy on GPU quota usage as a fraction of the limit.
options.C: Enable the Compute Engine API again in each region.
options.D: Check usage on the Quotas & System Limits page.
options.E: Create a budget for GPU spending with an alert at 80%.

explanation.summary: Quota usage and limits are exposed as Cloud Monitoring metrics and on the Quotas page. An alerting policy on usage divided by limit warns at 80% before jobs fail.

option_breakdown.A: Audit logs record API calls; they don't track quota usage against limits.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The policy fires when usage crosses 80% of the GPU quota.
option_breakdown.C: Re-enabling an API doesn't change quotas or show usage.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The Quotas page lists each quota with its current usage and limit.
option_breakdown.E: A budget tracks money, not how close usage is to a quota limit.

explanation.gcloud_command:
# Console > Monitoring > Alerting > Create policy > metric serviceruntime.googleapis.com/quota/allocation/usage
#   ratio to quota/limit, threshold 0.8

questions.title: A development change that broke production
questions.summary: Routes and firewall rules belong to a VPC, so separate Shared VPC host projects for production and non-production isolate their changes.
questions.question: Arden Mutual has one Shared VPC host project with one VPC network, holding production and development subnets. A developer with network admin rights on the host project widened a firewall rule for a test, and it exposed production VMs. Security wants development network changes to be unable to affect production at all. What should you do?

options.A: Create separate production and non-production host projects, each with its own VPC.
options.B: Add IAM conditions that limit the developer to rules whose names start with dev-.
options.C: Move the development subnets into a second VPC in the same host project.
options.D: Use network tags so development rules target only development VMs.

explanation.summary: Firewall rules and routes are resources of a VPC network, and IAM is granted per host project. Separate host projects with separate VPCs mean non-production administrators have no rights and no rules that touch production.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Separate host projects separate both the networks and who administers them, which is Google's recommended foundation.
option_breakdown.B: Name conditions are fragile, and the developer could still create a rule with any target in the shared VPC.
option_breakdown.C: A second VPC separates rules, but the same host-project admins still control both networks.
option_breakdown.D: Tags are chosen by whoever writes the rule, so nothing stops a rule targeting production VMs.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute shared-vpc enable net-host-prod
gcloud compute shared-vpc enable net-host-nonprod

questions.title: Developers with full rights in development only
questions.summary: Projects are the boundary for IAM, quota and billing, so production and non-production belong in separate projects, usually under separate folders.
questions.question: Quarry Lane Software runs development and production in one project, where developers are Editors. Developers must keep broad rights in development but have none in production, production must not share quota with load tests, and finance wants each environment's cost separately. What should you do?

options.A: Label every resource with env=dev or env=prod and add IAM conditions on that label.
options.B: Create a deny policy that denies developers every permission on resources labelled env=prod.
options.C: Move production into its own project in a production folder, and grant developers Editor only on the development project.
options.D: Put production resources in a separate region and restrict developers with an organisation policy on locations.

explanation.summary: IAM, quota and billing reports all follow the project. Separate projects under environment folders give developers rights in development only, keep quota apart and show each environment's cost without perfect labelling.

option_breakdown.A: Labels can be edited by the people they would restrict, and they don't separate quota.
option_breakdown.B: Deny policies can't target resources by label like this, and the shared quota and billing remain.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A project per environment is the boundary for access, quota and cost, as Google's foundation design recommends.
option_breakdown.D: Location policies restrict where resources are created, not who may change them, and quota is still shared.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager folders create --display-name=production --organization=ORG_ID
gcloud projects create quarry-prod --folder=FOLDER_ID

questions.title: An Admin console edit that the next sync undoes
questions.summary: Google Cloud Directory Sync is one-way from the LDAP directory, so changes must be made in Active Directory; edits in Cloud Identity are overwritten at the next sync.
questions.question: Linfield College syncs users and groups from on-premises Active Directory to Cloud Identity with Google Cloud Directory Sync every hour. An administrator corrected a user's department in the Google Admin console, but an hour later the old value was back. What should the administrator do?

options.A: Make the change in Active Directory, which Directory Sync treats as the source.
options.B: Enable two-way synchronisation in Directory Sync's configuration.
options.C: Lock the user's profile in the Admin console so syncs skip it.
options.D: Stop Directory Sync, make the change, and start it again.

explanation.summary: Directory Sync copies from Active Directory to Cloud Identity and never the other way, so every run makes Cloud Identity match Active Directory again.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Active Directory is the authoritative source; the change belongs there and the next sync carries it over.
option_breakdown.B: Directory Sync is one-way by design; it never writes back to Active Directory.
option_breakdown.C: There is no such lock; synced attributes follow the source directory.
option_breakdown.D: The next run after restarting would overwrite the change again.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Edit the user in Active Directory; the next Directory Sync run updates Cloud Identity

questions.title: Active Directory passwords that must never reach Google
questions.summary: Directory Sync creates the accounts; SAML single sign-on against AD FS lets users sign in with their Active Directory credentials without Google storing passwords.
questions.question: Users at Moreton Water are synced from Active Directory to Cloud Identity with Google Cloud Directory Sync. They must sign in to the Google Cloud console with their Active Directory passwords, and security forbids storing those passwords or their hashes at Google. What should you add?

options.A: Password synchronisation from the domain controllers to Cloud Identity.
options.B: SAML single sign-on with AD FS as the identity provider.
options.C: A workforce identity pool that replaces the synced accounts.
options.D: Two-step verification on every Cloud Identity account.

explanation.summary: With SAML single sign-on, Cloud Identity redirects sign-in to AD FS, which checks the Active Directory password. Directory Sync keeps providing the accounts, and no password leaves the company.

option_breakdown.A: Password synchronisation copies password hashes to Google, which security forbids.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. AD FS authenticates users against Active Directory, so Google never holds their passwords.
option_breakdown.C: Workforce Identity Federation avoids Cloud Identity accounts altogether; the company already chose synced accounts.
option_breakdown.D: Two-step verification adds a factor but users would still need a password stored at Google.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Admin console > Security > SSO with third-party IdP: AD FS sign-in URL and certificate

questions.title: Single sign-on works, but new hires have no account
questions.summary: SAML single sign-on only authenticates; Cloud Identity accounts must still exist, which automatic provisioning from Microsoft Entra ID creates and suspends.
questions.question: Hallam Studios configured SAML single sign-on from Microsoft Entra ID to Cloud Identity. Existing employees sign in to Google Cloud without problems, but this month's new hires get an error that their account doesn't exist. Accounts were created by hand until now. What should you set up?

options.A: Google Cloud Directory Sync on a domain controller.
options.B: A longer SAML session lifetime in Entra ID.
options.C: A workforce identity pool for the new hires only.
options.D: Automatic user provisioning from Entra ID's Google Cloud enterprise app.

explanation.summary: Single sign-on checks who a user is but doesn't create Cloud Identity accounts. Entra ID's provisioning creates, updates and suspends them automatically as employees join and leave.

option_breakdown.A: The company has no on-premises Active Directory for Directory Sync to read.
option_breakdown.B: Session length doesn't create accounts that don't exist.
option_breakdown.C: A separate federation model for some employees splits identity management for no reason.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Automatic provisioning creates new hires' Cloud Identity accounts, and single sign-on then works for them.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Entra ID > Enterprise applications > Google Cloud > Provisioning: set mode Automatic

questions.title: Federated employees signing in every hour
questions.summary: A workforce pool's session duration sets how long console and gcloud sessions last, from 15 minutes to 12 hours.
questions.question: Employees at Carrick Energy reach Google Cloud through a workforce identity pool federated with Okta. They complain that they must sign in again every hour. Security accepts sessions of up to eight hours. What should you change?

options.A: The pool's session duration, to 28800s.
options.B: The OAuth access-token lifetime organisation policy, to eight hours.
options.C: The Google Workspace session length for all users.
options.D: The expiry of the IAM role bindings granted to the pool.

explanation.summary: The workforce pool's session duration controls how long its console and gcloud sessions stay valid, and it can be set between 15 minutes and 12 hours.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Eight hours, 28800 seconds, is within the pool setting's range and applies only to that pool.
option_breakdown.B: That policy extends service-account access tokens, not federated users' sessions.
option_breakdown.C: Workspace session settings apply to Cloud Identity users, not to federated identities in a workforce pool.
option_breakdown.D: Binding expiry removes access at a date; it doesn't change how long a sign-in lasts.

questions.title: A role for every federated user in one department
questions.summary: Workforce identities can be granted roles by a mapped attribute with a principalSet identifier of the form …/workforcePools/POOL/attribute.ATTRIBUTE/VALUE.
questions.question: A workforce pool named staff-pool maps the identity provider's department claim to attribute.department. Everyone whose department is finance must get BigQuery Data Viewer on project fin-reports, including people who join later. Which member should the binding use?

options.A: A group: member named finance@ in the company's domain.
options.B: A principal member for each finance user's subject.
options.C: A principalSet member for the pool's attribute.department/finance.
options.D: A domain: member for the identity provider's domain.

explanation.summary: A principalSet identifier can select every identity in a workforce pool with a given mapped attribute value, so one binding covers current and future finance staff.

option_breakdown.A: Federated identities have no Cloud Identity group unless one is mapped; a domain group doesn't contain them.
option_breakdown.B: Per-user bindings miss people who join later and must be maintained by hand.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/staff-pool/attribute.department/finance covers every matching identity.
option_breakdown.D: A domain member names a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity domain, not identities in a workforce pool.

questions.title: A role for one federated user
questions.summary: A single workforce identity is named by its subject: principal://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL/subject/SUBJECT.
questions.question: One contractor signs in through the workforce pool vendor-pool, and the provider maps the contractor's ID to google.subject as c-4471. The contractor alone needs Logs Viewer on project ops-prod. Which member should the binding use?

options.A: A user: member with the contractor's email address.
options.B: A principal member for vendor-pool's subject c-4471.
options.C: A principalSet member for all identities in vendor-pool.
options.D: A serviceAccount: member that the contractor impersonates.

explanation.summary: IAM names one federated workforce identity with a principal identifier built from the pool and the mapped google.subject.

option_breakdown.A: user: members are Google accounts; a federated contractor has no Google account.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. principal://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/vendor-pool/subject/c-4471 is exactly that contractor.
option_breakdown.C: Granting the whole pool gives every vendor identity the role, not one contractor.
