option_breakdown.D: A shared service account hides who acted and isn't needed for a federated user.

questions.title: A firewall rule's settings from two months ago
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory history covers about five weeks; older configuration changes are found in Admin Activity audit logs, which are kept for 400 days.
questions.question: An auditor at Harrow Bank asks what the firewall rule allow-partner allowed eight weeks ago, before two changes were made to it. No asset exports or feeds were ever set up, and no log sinks exist. Where can you find the changes?

options.A: The rule's asset history in Cloud Asset Inventory.
options.B: Firewall Rules Logging for the rule.
options.C: VPC Flow Logs from that period.
options.D: The Admin Activity audit log entries for the rule.

explanation.summary: Admin Activity audit logs record every change to a firewall rule, with the request, and are kept for 400 days. Asset history covers only the last five weeks.

option_breakdown.A: Asset history reaches back about five weeks, so eight weeks ago is out of range.
option_breakdown.B: Firewall Rules Logging records connections the rule matched, not changes to its configuration.
option_breakdown.C: Flow logs record traffic samples and must have been enabled at the time.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The rule's patch and update entries in Admin Activity logs show what changed and when, for 400 days.

questions.title: No one may delete the network host project
questions.summary: An IAM deny policy denying cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/projects.delete stops anyone, Owners included, from deleting a project.
questions.question: Deleting the Shared VPC host project at Ingram Logistics would take down every service project's network. Several administrators hold Owner on it. Using generally available features only, how do you stop anyone from deleting the project, Owners included?

options.A: Remove the Owner role from everyone and grant Editor instead.
options.B: A deny policy on the project that denies the projects.delete permission.
options.C: An organisation policy that restricts resource locations for the project.
options.D: A budget with a 100% threshold that alerts the network team.

explanation.summary: Deny policies are evaluated before allow policies, so a deny rule for cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/projects.delete blocks deletion whatever roles a principal holds.

option_breakdown.A: Editor can't delete a project, but removing Owner from everyone also removes the administrators' ability to run the project.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A deny rule on projects.delete stops every principal it names, including Owners, and it is GA.
option_breakdown.C: A location policy limits where resources are created, not whether the project can be deleted.
option_breakdown.D: A budget watches spending; it can't block an action.

questions.title: US workloads that need FedRAMP High controls
questions.summary: Assured Workloads applies a regulatory control package, such as FedRAMP High, to a folder: US data location, US-person support personnel and allowed services.
questions.question: A contractor at Halsey Federal will host a US government system that must meet FedRAMP High: data stored only in the United States, support access only by US persons with enhanced background checks, and only services authorised at that level. What should you set up?

options.A: An Assured Workloads folder with the FedRAMP High control package.
options.B: The gcp.resourceLocations organisation policy set to in:us-locations.
options.C: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the system's projects.
options.D: Access Transparency logs reviewed weekly by the security team.

explanation.summary: Assured Workloads' FedRAMP High package enforces US data location, restricts support personnel and limits the folder to authorised services, and it monitors for violations.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The control package covers data location, personnel access and service restrictions together.
option_breakdown.B: A location policy covers where data lives, not who at Google may access it or which services are authorised.
option_breakdown.C: A perimeter limits data movement through Google APIs; it doesn't control location or personnel.
option_breakdown.D: Access Transparency shows access after it happens; it doesn't restrict who can access.

questions.title: A project outside the Assured Workloads folder
questions.summary: Assured Workloads controls apply to the projects in its folder; a project created elsewhere in the organisation gets none of them.
questions.question: Corwen Health created an Assured Workloads folder with the EU Data Boundary and Support package. A team then created a project directly under the organisation and deployed patient data to us-central1 without any error. Why was nothing blocked?

options.A: The package only alerts on violations and never blocks anything.
options.B: The package's controls take 30 days to start applying.
options.C: The controls apply only to projects in the Assured Workloads folder.
options.D: us-central1 is allowed by the EU Data Boundary package for backups.

explanation.summary: Assured Workloads enforces its package with organisation policies on its folder, so only projects created inside that folder inherit the controls.

option_breakdown.A: The package enforces controls such as resource locations through organisation policies, and also monitors for violations.
option_breakdown.B: Controls apply as soon as the folder exists; there is no waiting period.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A project at the organisation root inherits nothing from the folder, so EU-only locations didn't apply to it.
option_breakdown.D: The EU packages restrict resources to EU locations; us-central1 is outside them.

questions.title: Finding out when an Assured Workloads control is overridden
questions.summary: Assured Workloads monitors its folder for organisation policy and resource violations and can email notifications when they happen.
questions.question: An administrator at Lyle Defence with Organization Policy Administrator could change a policy inside the company's Assured Workloads folder. The compliance team wants to know whenever such a change breaks the control package, without building anything. What should you use?

options.A: A budget alert on the folder's projects.
options.B: Assured Workloads violation monitoring, with email notifications.
options.C: A Cloud Asset Inventory export to BigQuery every month.
options.D: Personalized Service Health alerts for the folder.

explanation.summary: Assured Workloads watches its folder for changes that break the package's organisation policies or resource rules, lists them as violations and can notify by email.

option_breakdown.A: Budgets watch spending, not policy changes.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Violation monitoring reports policy and resource violations in the folder and sends notifications.
option_breakdown.C: A monthly export is a snapshot to analyse later, not a notification when a control is broken.
option_breakdown.D: Personalized Service Health reports Google Cloud incidents, not your own policy changes.

questions.title: Where a Spanner configuration keeps its replicas
questions.summary: Describing a Spanner instance configuration lists its replicas, their types and regions, and its default leader region.
questions.question: An architect at Selby Payments is choosing a Spanner multi-region configuration. Before deciding, they need to know which regions hold read-write replicas and which region is the default leader in the configuration eur5. What is the most direct way to find out?

options.A: List the Compute Engine zones in each European region.
options.B: Create a test instance in eur5 and read its monitoring charts.
options.C: Describe the eur5 instance configuration.
options.D: Read the Spanner API's quota page for the project.

explanation.summary: An instance configuration lists its replicas with their types and locations and its default leader. Describing it answers the question without creating anything.

option_breakdown.A: Zones say where Compute Engine runs, not where a Spanner configuration places replicas.
option_breakdown.B: A test instance costs money and still doesn't show the configuration's replica layout directly.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. gcloud spanner instance-configs describe eur5 shows each replica's type and region and the default leader.
option_breakdown.D: Quotas limit capacity; they say nothing about replica placement.

questions.title: Where namespace costs appear after cost allocation
questions.summary: With GKE cost allocation enabled, namespace and Kubernetes label costs appear in the detailed usage cost export to BigQuery.
questions.question: Finance at Hawley Insurance enabled GKE cost allocation on a shared cluster. It now wants to query cost by Kubernetes namespace with SQL. Where should it look?

options.A: The standard usage cost export to BigQuery.
options.B: The detailed usage cost export to BigQuery.
options.C: The cluster's Workloads page in the console.
options.D: A budget scoped to the cluster's project.

explanation.summary: Cost allocation adds namespace and Kubernetes label information to resource-level rows, which only the detailed usage cost export contains.

option_breakdown.A: The standard export aggregates by service and SKU, without the resource-level rows cost allocation adds to.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The detailed export carries the namespace and label breakdown that SQL can group by.
option_breakdown.C: The Workloads page shows resource requests and status, not billed cost.
option_breakdown.D: A budget alerts on a total; it doesn't break cost down by namespace.

questions.title: Why the bill went up, without SQL
questions.summary: Cloud Billing reports chart cost by project, service or SKU over time and compare periods, with no SQL; Billing Account Viewer is enough to see them.
questions.question: A manager at Thursby Media has Billing Account Viewer and asks why last month's bill was 30% higher than the month before, and which projects and services drove it. They don't write SQL, and only generally available features may be used. What should they use?

options.A: The detailed billing export, queried in BigQuery.
options.B: A budget with alerts at 50%, 90% and 100%.
options.C: Cloud Billing reports, grouped by project and then by service, comparing the two months.
options.D: The Cost Table filtered by invoice month, exported to CSV.

explanation.summary: Billing reports chart cost over time grouped by project, service or SKU, and can compare periods, so the manager sees what grew without writing queries.

option_breakdown.A: The export answers the question but needs SQL, which the manager doesn't write.
option_breakdown.B: A budget alerts about future spending; it doesn't explain last month's increase.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Grouping the reports by project and by service shows which ones grew between the two months.
option_breakdown.D: The cost table lists invoice lines, but comparing two months in a spreadsheet is the slow way.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Billing > Reports: Group by Project, then Service; time range: last two months

questions.title: Stopping a sandbox's charges when its budget runs out
questions.summary: Budgets only notify. To stop charges, publish budget notifications to Pub/Sub and have a function disable billing on the project.
questions.question: Students at Ellery College each get a sandbox project with a $50 budget. When a project's actual spend reaches the budget, all its charges must stop automatically, even if the sandbox is lost. Nobody watches the alert emails. What should you configure?

options.A: Lower Compute Engine CPU and Cloud Storage quotas in each project to match the budget.
options.B: A spending limit on the billing account, applied to each sandbox project separately.
options.C: A budget per project that emails the course administrators at 50%, 90% and 100% of the amount.
options.D: Budget notifications to Pub/Sub, and a function that disables billing on the project at 100%.

explanation.summary: A Cloud Billing budget sends notifications but never caps spend by itself. Programmatic notifications to Pub/Sub can trigger a function that unlinks the project's billing account, which stops billable services, so data in the project may be lost.

option_breakdown.A: Quotas limit some resources but not every billable service, so charges could still exceed $50.
option_breakdown.B: Cloud Billing has no per-project spending limit to set; budgets are the cost-control tool, and they only notify.
option_breakdown.C: Emails only inform people, and the stem says nobody acts on them, so charges continue.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The function reacts to the budget's Pub/Sub message and disables billing on the project, which stops its charges.

questions.title: No public buckets, but partners still get access
questions.summary: Public access prevention blocks allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers on every bucket; uniform bucket-level access turns ACLs off; neither blocks named external accounts.
questions.question: Across every project in Brennock Health's organization, no Cloud Storage bucket or object may ever be made public, and object ACLs must not be usable to grant access. Some buckets are shared with named accounts at partner companies' own domains, and that must keep working. Which two organization policy constraints should you enforce? (Choose two.)

options.A: gcp.resourceLocations, limited to EU locations
options.B: storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess
options.C: iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains, limited to Brennock's customer ID
options.D: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation

explanation.summary: Public access prevention stops any grant to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers on buckets and objects. Enforcing uniform bucket-level access disables ACLs, so access is only through IAM. Neither restricts grants to named partner accounts.

option_breakdown.A: Resource locations control where data lives, not who may read it.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. With uniform bucket-level access enforced, ACLs can't grant access to anything.
option_breakdown.C: Domain restricted sharing would block public access too, but it also blocks the partners' accounts from other domains, which must keep working.
option_breakdown.D: Blocking key creation is a credential control; it doesn't stop a bucket being made public.
option_breakdown.E: Correct. It blocks public access on every bucket under the organization, whatever IAM or ACLs say.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager org-policies enable-enforce storage.publicAccessPrevention --organization=ORG_ID
gcloud resource-manager org-policies enable-enforce storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess --organization=ORG_ID

questions.title: Autoscaling stopped by a regional CPU quota
questions.summary: A managed instance group that can't add VMs because of a regional quota needs a higher quota in that region, requested through Cloud Quotas.
questions.question: During a sale, Marlow Retail's regional managed instance group in us-central1 stops at 24 VMs although the autoscaler's maximum is 60. The group's errors show that the regional CPUS quota is exceeded. Other regions have spare quota, but the application must stay in us-central1. What should you do?

options.A: Raise the autoscaler's maximum number of instances to 120.
options.B: Request a higher CPUS quota for us-central1 through Cloud Quotas.
options.C: Move the project to a different billing account with a higher credit limit.
options.D: Disable and re-enable the Compute Engine API to reset the quota usage.

explanation.summary: Quotas cap how many resources a project may use in each region. When the autoscaler is blocked by a quota rather than by its own limit, the fix is a quota increase in that region.

option_breakdown.A: The autoscaler isn't the limit; it already wants more VMs than the quota allows.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A larger regional CPUS quota lets the group grow past 24 VMs in us-central1.
option_breakdown.C: Quotas belong to the project and region, not to the billing account's credit.
option_breakdown.D: Quota usage reflects running resources; re-enabling the API doesn't change it and risks disrupting the service.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > IAM & Admin > Quotas & System Limits > CPUs (us-central1) > Edit quota

questions.title: Switching between two projects' gcloud settings
questions.summary: Named gcloud configurations hold a project, account and default region or zone each, and you activate one to switch them all at once.
questions.question: A support engineer at Tavish Telecom manages VMs in project billing-prod in europe-west2 and project lab-sandbox in us-east1, using a different account for each. Twice this month a command ran against the wrong project. The engineer wants to switch the project, account, region and zone together with one command. What should you recommend?

options.A: Install a second copy of the gcloud CLI for the second project.
options.B: Run gcloud init again each time the engineer changes project.
options.C: Create a named gcloud configuration for each project, and activate the one needed.
options.D: Add --project to every command and set the region in an environment variable.

explanation.summary: A gcloud configuration is a named set of properties such as account, project, compute/region and compute/zone. Activating one switches all of them in one step.

option_breakdown.A: A second installation is unnecessary; one gcloud supports many named configurations.
option_breakdown.B: Re-running init each time is slow and error-prone, which is how the mistakes happen.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. One configuration per project holds its account, project, region and zone; activating it switches them together.
option_breakdown.D: Per-command flags are exactly what gets forgotten, and they leave the account unchanged.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud config configurations create billing-prod
gcloud config set project billing-prod
gcloud config set compute/region europe-west2
gcloud config configurations activate lab-sandbox

questions.title: Contractors signing in with their own company's Okta
questions.summary: Workforce Identity Federation lets users from an external identity provider use the console with IAM roles granted to pool principals, without Cloud Identity accounts.
questions.question: Harlow Engineering hires 300 contractors from a partner whose staff sign in with the partner's Okta. The contractors need read access to BigQuery datasets in one project through the console. Harlow must not create Cloud Identity or Workspace accounts for them, and access must end when the partner disables an account. What should you do?

options.A: Create a workforce pool with an Okta provider, and grant BigQuery Data Viewer to the contractors' group in it.
options.B: Create one service account for all the contractors and share a key for it with the partner.
options.C: Create a workload identity pool with an OIDC provider that trusts the partner's Okta tenant.
options.D: Create a Cloud Identity account for each contractor, kept in sync from the partner's Okta directory.

explanation.summary: A workforce identity pool trusts an external identity provider for human users. IAM roles go to pool principals, such as everyone in a mapped group, and a disabled account at the provider can no longer sign in.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The pool federates the partner's Okta for people, and the principal set grant gives the group read access.
option_breakdown.B: A shared key has no per-person identity and doesn't end when a contractor leaves.
option_breakdown.C: Workload identity pools are for software workloads, not people signing in to the console.
option_breakdown.D: Synced Cloud Identity accounts are exactly what Harlow must not create.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud iam workforce-pools create partner-pool --organization=ORG_ID --location=global
gcloud iam workforce-pools providers create-oidc okta --workforce-pool=partner-pool --location=global \
  --issuer-uri=https://partner.okta.com --client-id=CLIENT_ID --attribute-mapping=google.subject=assertion.sub,google.groups=assertion.groups

questions.title: Cost per team across shared projects
questions.summary: Labels on resources travel into the Cloud Billing export, so costs can be grouped by team in BigQuery even when teams share projects.
questions.question: At Wexcombe Media, four teams share the same three projects, and finance needs a monthly cost total per team for Compute Engine, Cloud Storage and BigQuery, queryable in SQL. Moving teams into separate projects is not an option this year. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Add a team tag to each VM's network tags.
options.B: Create a separate billing account for each team.
options.C: Apply a team label to every VM, bucket and dataset.
options.D: Enable the Cloud Billing export to BigQuery and group the cost rows by the team label.
options.E: Create a budget per project with alerts to each team's lead.

explanation.summary: Resource labels are copied into each cost row of the billing export. With the export in BigQuery, finance can sum cost by the team label across the shared projects.

option_breakdown.A: Network tags only select VMs for firewall rules and routes; they never show up in Cloud Billing data.
option_breakdown.B: A project links to one billing account, so separate accounts would mean separate projects, which is ruled out.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Labels are how costs from shared projects are attributed to teams.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The BigQuery export carries the labels, so a GROUP BY on the team label gives the totals.
option_breakdown.E: Budgets alert on a project's spend; they don't split one project's cost between teams.

questions.title: Access that follows people as they join and leave
questions.summary: Grant IAM roles to Google groups managed in Cloud Identity, so that joining or leaving the group changes access without editing IAM policies.
questions.question: At Cresswell Bakeries, about ten analysts join or leave the data team each month, and each time someone edits IAM bindings on four projects by hand, often forgetting one. The team's access should change as soon as HR updates the team's membership in Cloud Identity. What should you do?

options.A: Give each analyst a service account key that carries the roles the data team needs.
options.B: Grant each analyst the roles individually, with a script that HR runs once a month.
options.C: Grant the roles to the company's whole Cloud Identity domain on the four projects.
options.D: Grant the roles on the four projects to a Google group for the data team.

explanation.summary: IAM bindings on a group apply to everyone in it. Adding or removing a member changes their access everywhere the group is granted, with no IAM edits.

option_breakdown.A: Keys are long-lived secrets tied to a service account, not to a person.
option_breakdown.B: A monthly script still leaves people with access for weeks after they leave.
option_breakdown.C: Granting the domain gives every employee the access, not just the data team.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The bindings are set once, and membership changes do the rest.

questions.title: No external IPs except on the bastion
questions.summary: The compute.vmExternalIpAccess list constraint allows external IPs only on the VM instances you list.
questions.question: Security at Ravenhill Water wants no Compute Engine VM anywhere in the organization to have an external IP address, except one bastion VM named bastion-1 in project net-hub. Developers in other projects must be unable to add one, even with Compute Admin. What should you do?

options.A: Create a firewall rule in each VPC that denies all ingress from 0.0.0.0/0.
options.B: Remove Compute Admin from developers and grant Compute Viewer.
options.C: Set the compute.vmExternalIpAccess constraint at the organization to allow only bastion-1.
options.D: Enable Private Google Access on every subnet.

explanation.summary: Organization policies apply whatever IAM roles people hold. The compute.vmExternalIpAccess list constraint permits external IPs only on the instances in its allowed list.

option_breakdown.A: Deny rules block traffic, but VMs could still be given external IPs, which is what's forbidden.
option_breakdown.B: Removing roles stops developers' work on VMs, and service accounts could still create VMs with external IPs.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The constraint blocks external IPs on every VM except bastion-1, regardless of IAM roles.
option_breakdown.D: Private Google Access lets private VMs reach Google APIs; it doesn't prevent external IPs.

explanation.gcloud_command:
# policy.yaml: constraint compute.vmExternalIpAccess, allowedValues:
#   projects/net-hub/zones/ZONE/instances/bastion-1
gcloud org-policies set-policy policy.yaml

questions.title: Separating production from everything else
questions.summary: Folders group projects so that IAM grants and organization policies set once on a folder apply to all its projects.
questions.question: Ollerton Group has just created its organization and has 40 projects directly under it. Production projects need stricter organization policies and a different set of admin groups than development and test projects, and new projects should pick up the right settings from where they are created. What should you do?

options.A: Create a second organization that holds only the production projects and their admins.
options.B: Create Production and Non-production folders, move the projects in, and set policies there.
options.C: Label every project env=prod or env=dev, and set the policies and roles by label.
options.D: Set each policy and IAM binding directly on every project, according to its environment.

explanation.summary: Organization policies and IAM allow policies are inherited down the hierarchy. Folders let each environment get its own settings once, and a project created in a folder inherits them.

option_breakdown.A: A second organization splits identity, billing and policies and makes shared administration harder.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Each folder carries its environment's policies and admin groups, and new projects inherit them.
option_breakdown.C: Labels are metadata for filtering and billing; IAM and organization policies aren't set by project label.
option_breakdown.D: Per-project settings work but must be repeated for every new project, which is error-prone.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager folders create --display-name=Production --organization=ORG_ID
gcloud beta projects move PROJECT_ID --folder=FOLDER_ID

questions.title: Self-service projects only in one folder and in the EU
questions.summary: Grant Project Creator on the folder, and set the resource locations constraint on the same folder; both are inherited by the projects created there and affect nobody else.
questions.question: The data team may create its own projects, but only inside the folder data-eng, and every resource in those projects must be created in EU locations. Other teams must not be affected. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Grant the data team the Project Creator role on the data-eng folder.
options.B: Set the resource locations policy on the data-eng folder to in:eu-locations.
options.C: Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter around the projects in data-eng.
options.D: Set the resource locations policy on the organization to in:eu-locations.
options.E: Grant the data team the Project Creator role on the organization node.

explanation.summary: IAM grants and organization policies are both inherited down the hierarchy. Setting both on the folder scopes them to the data team's projects.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A folder-level grant lets the team create projects there and nowhere else.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The constraint applies to every project in the folder, and only there.
option_breakdown.C: A perimeter limits API data movement; it doesn't control where resources are created.
option_breakdown.D: An organization-level constraint would restrict every other team as well.
option_breakdown.E: An organization-level grant lets the team create projects anywhere in the organization.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager folders add-iam-policy-binding FOLDER_ID \
  --member=group:data-team@example.com --role=roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator
gcloud resource-manager org-policies allow gcp.resourceLocations in:eu-locations --folder=FOLDER_ID
